bug_semantics: The Relay server exposes FastAPI endpoints that deserialize attacker-supplied, base64-encoded pickle payloads without authentication or integrity checks: the /_call endpoint's lazyllm_call() handler decodes call_args/call_kwargs via load_obj() (cloudpickle.loads) and the Global-Parameters header via globals.unpickle_and_update_data() (str2obj -> pickle.loads), while /generate decodes the request body and headers through decode_request() (pickle.loads). Unpickle of a crafted payload instantiates attacker-chosen Python objects and executes arbitrary code on the deployment server (CWE-20 improper input validation leading to unsafe deserialization); the attack is launched remotely by anyone who can reach the server port.
flaw_origin: Commit 1289fd08aa192543fea8239ab1225a33daa7cab2 ("add processer service (#519)", 2025-06-03, author wangzhihong <wangzhihong@sensetime.com>) first added the /_call endpoint with the lazyllm_call function named by the advisory: `fname, args, kwargs = await request.json(); args, kwargs = load_obj(args), load_obj(kwargs); r = getattr(func, fname)(*args, **kwargs)`, where load_obj() performs cloudpickle.loads on attacker-controlled base64 data. The parent tree (ae8c505a296a1706f09b052a0998b83e1d71c88b) contains zero occurrences of lazyllm_call. The deserialization-from-network pattern it instantiates is the culmination of the same pattern introduced earlier in the file (45d11f9a 2024-04-23 added pickle.loads of the request body; 78452a43 2024-07-10 added decode_request/unpickle of the Global-Parameters header), so /_call is the advisory-named introducer and the file-wide pattern its ancestry.
ai_marker: absent — the BIC commit object names author and committer wangzhihong <wangzhihong@sensetime.com> (2025-06-03), message "add processer service (#519)"; no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or bot/AI identity anywhere on the object.
evidence: Advisory (CVE-2025-10965 / GHSA-4c22-7xx9-4rpv, VulDB id 325833, upstream issue LazyAGI/LazyLLM#764): the function lazyllm_call of the file lazyllm/components/deploy/relay/server.py in LazyLLM up to 0.6.1 leads to deserialization; the attack can be launched remotely and the exploit is publicly disclosed.

Vulnerable state at HEAD (post-v1.3.0a1, 26c9d4d0): `lazyllm_call` at src line 101+ decodes `Global-Parameters` header via globals.unpickle_and_update_data() (lazyllm/common/globals.py:208 -> str2obj -> lazyllm/common/utils.py:150 `pickle.loads(base64.b64decode(...))`) and `call_args, call_kwargs = load_obj(call_args), load_obj(call_kwargs)` (lazyllm/common/utils.py:240 -> cloudpickle.loads). The only gate is the optional static Security-Key header comparison added 2025-10-23 (00b7ba82, #796), which is absent by default (empty key passes), not a deserialization fix.

BIC creation check: `git log --all -S 'async def lazyllm_call'` and the file history pin the /_call endpoint's introduction to 1289fd08aa192543fea8239ab1225a33daa7cab2 (PR #519); `git show ae8c505a:lazyllm/components/deploy/relay/server.py | grep -c lazyllm_call` = 0, so the advisory-named function does not exist in the parent tree (introducer_parent_absent=true).

Earlier ancestry of the pattern: 45d11f9ade70955d314ed5fd6594e42d7deb47f1 (2024-04-23) introduced `input = pickle.loads(codecs.decode(input.encode('utf-8'), 'base64'))` on the /generate request body (first ships v0.1.2); 78452a43808960cfbea74276be9e8de89b085a9e (2024-07-10) introduced decode_request() on the Global-Parameters header (lazyllm/common/globals.py:98 `pickle.loads`). These are the file-wide deserialization ancestors; 1289fd08 is the advisory-named introducer of lazyllm_call.

No fix in repository: `git log --all -i --grep='deserial|pickle.*secur'` shows no deserialization hardening; at HEAD lazyllm_call still unpickles header and JSON-controlled arguments; tags v0.6.x-v1.3.0a1 (spanning the advisory's 'up to 0.6.1' and later) contain the vulnerable endpoint. Hence fix_sha/direct_fix_sha are null (unpatched as of audit date).

AI-marker screening: `git log --format='%an <%ae>%n%cn <%ce>%n%B' -1 1289fd08` shows only the human identity wangzhihong and the one-line feature message; no claude/copilot/anthropic/openai/generated/co-authored marker on the BIC object (same screening negative for ancestors 45d11f9a and 78452a43).

ppa re-checked line-level 2026-08-29 against clone history: git show ae8c505a:lazyllm/components/deploy/relay/server.py already wires /generate with decode_request(request.headers.get('Global-Parameters')) and decode_request of the JSON body (lines 68-72), and git show ae8c505a:lazyllm/common/globals.py:101 defines str2obj as pickle.loads(base64.b64decode(...)), so the unauthenticated-pickle-deserialization sink is already present at the parent; only the /_call endpoint lines are new. -> introducer_parent_absent=false.
reasoning: Vulnerability first: the advisory names lazyllm_call in server.py as the deserialization sink; the code confirms it decodes base64 attacker JSON into cloudpickle.loads/pickle.loads with no authentication by default. BIC choice: the commit that first wrote the advisory-named function is 1289fd08 (PR #519, 2025-06-03); its parent lacks the function entirely, making the /_call introduction the BIC for this case. The earlier body/header pickle.loads (45d11f9a, 78452a43) are the same pattern's ancestry and are documented as such rather than as the introducer, because the advisory scopes the flaw to lazyllm_call. The 2025-10-23 Security-Key check (00b7ba82) is an opt-in gate, not a deserialization fix, and HEAD still unpickles input — so the case is unpatched and fix_sha is null. Squash check: PR #519 is a single cohesive feature commit (processor service endpoints with matching client-side plumbing), not a decomposed multi-feature squash; squash_decomposed=false. AI decision: BIC-only attribution — the 2025 commit object carries only human identities with no AI marker, so NOT_AI.
remaining_gap: No upstream fix exists as of the audit date (HEAD 26c9d4d0 still deserializes attacker-controlled data in lazyllm_call and /generate); fix_sha/direct_fix_sha are null and should be backfilled when the project ships a remediation.

unpatched.reason: No upstream fix exists as of the audit date; HEAD 26c9d4d0 still deserializes attacker-controlled base64 payloads in lazyllm_call and /generate.

potential_fix.approach: Replace pickle-based deserialization of client payloads with a restricted format (JSON) and, where pickle is required, deserialize inside a sandboxed, allowlisted-class loader with authentication on the Relay endpoints.
potential_fix.rationale: Removing unrestricted pickle deserialization eliminates the code-execution primitive regardless of endpoint exposure.
